title: Slices With Sum Divisible by K
statement:
Given an integer array nums and a positive integer k, count the non-empty contiguous slices of nums whose sum is a multiple of k. Zero is a multiple of every k, and so are negative multiples like -6 for k = 3.

Slices at different positions count separately, even if they hold the same values.

examples.why: Only [-2, 5], with sum 3. Note that -2 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 3, not -2.
All six slices sum to 0, which every k divides.

hints: The sum of slice i..j is prefix[j + 1] − prefix[i]. When is a difference of two numbers a multiple of k?
Exactly when both numbers leave the same remainder when divided by k. So count prefix sums by their remainder.

Walk the array keeping the running remainder. Each earlier prefix with the same remainder is one more slice ending here. Make negative remainders positive, and seed the count with remainder 0 for the empty prefix.

explain.intuition:
Write the slice sum as a difference of prefix sums: P[j] − P[i]. That is a multiple of k exactly when P[j] and P[i] have the same remainder mod k. So you never need the sums themselves, only how many earlier prefixes landed in each remainder bucket.

Walk once, keep a count per remainder, and for each new prefix add how many earlier prefixes share its remainder. The empty prefix (sum 0) counts too, which is how slices starting at index 0 get counted. In JavaScript and many other languages % keeps the sign, so -2 % 3 is -2, not 1. Normalise with ((s % k) + k) % k.
steps: For each x: sum = (sum + x) mod k, made non-negative.
pitfalls: Using the raw % result with negatives. Remainders -2 and 1 are the same class mod 3 but land in different buckets.
Forgetting the empty prefix, which misses every slice that starts at index 0.
Looking for an exact sum like the plain "slices that sum to k" problem. Here every multiple counts, including 0 and negatives.

solutions.title: Check every slice
solutions.idea: Fix the start, extend the end, and keep a running sum. Count the sums that divide evenly.

solutions.title: Count prefix remainders
solutions.idea: Two prefixes with the same remainder bound a slice whose sum divides evenly. Count remainders as you go.
